reason: The text portrays the Hebrews (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל - 'children of Israel') as a distinct people and nation multiple times. They are: (1) referred to as a collective national entity distinguished from Egypt ('בֵּין מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל' - between Egypt and Israel); (2) numbered as approximately 600,000 men plus families, livestock, and possessions, indicating a large, organized population far beyond a family unit; (3) depicted as a coordinated national body conducting organized departure with collective resources; (4) shown making national decisions and acting in unison (the entire people heeds Moses's instructions, takes possessions, and departs together). While the text also emphasizes their relationship to Yahweh and their role as followers/servants, this religious dimension does not negate their distinct portrayal as an organized nation with national identity and structures.
